methods: Verified the exact accepted COL26.8 usage and pinned accepted parent chain for COL ID 9M4BT.
Checked all 89 indexed dossier shards for COL ID, normalized scientific-name, and source DOI duplicates.
Searched repository source/data records and public GitHub issues and pull requests across all states for Physcomitrium patens, COL ID 9M4BT, and DOI 10.3389/fpls.2020.00643.
duplicateAudit.limitations: This audit covers the pinned COL26.8 registry, selected repository records, and public issue/PR search results at the checked time; it is not a claim that no other relevant research exists.

species.scope: Evidence is limited to a laboratory observation of stomatal-lineage cell development on Physcomitrium patens sporophyte epidermis. It does not establish the frequency of this division across plants, populations, or environments, and does not describe a field population.

lifeStatusScope.wild: The cited observation uses laboratory-grown wild-type strains under sterile culture, not a field observation of an unmanaged population.
lifeStatusScope.domesticated: Domesticated populations have not been assessed; laboratory culture alone is not treated as evidence of domestication.
lifeStatusScope.fossil: Fossil occurrence and geological age have not been assessed.

claims.text: In laboratory observations of Physcomitrium patens sporophyte epidermis, when two early guard mother cells formed adjacently, one had the potential to undergo an asymmetric spacing division that produced an epidermal spacer cell between the formerly adjacent cells. The illustrated division was followed over approximately two hours.
claims.locator: Results, ‘Stomatal Patterning and GMC Spacing Divisions,’ paragraphs 1–2; Figure 5 legend; the abstract summarizes the same conditional observation.
claims.placeTimeScope: Laboratory study published in 2020; sterile-cultured Physcomitrium patens wild-type strains Gransden 2004, Gransden D12, and Villersexel were used in the study. The Figure 5 cell sequence spans approximately two hours; no field locality or collection date is reported for that sequence.
claims.lifeStatus: Experimental sporophyte tissue from laboratory-grown wild-type moss strains; this is not an in-situ population observation, a domestication result, or fossil evidence.

gaps: The observation supports a conditional developmental possibility, not the frequency or prevalence of spacing divisions across strains, populations, or growth environments.
The authors could not track the dissected live samples for longer, and the later fate or renewed identity of the spacer cell remains unclear.
Life history, ecology, evolution, geographic distribution, fossils, conservation, systematic evidence search, and independent expert review remain unassessed.

completenessReasons: One conditional laboratory observation partially supports stomatal-lineage morphology and does not quantify its frequency or population variation.
The fate of the resulting spacer cell remains unresolved in the cited study.
Six other biological facets, a systematic source search, and independent expert review have not been completed.
